title: Ventana Biotech ops intake scratchpad
content:
Ventana Biotech — intake call notes (initial ops + infra capture)

Date: 2026-02-15 — quick follow-up captured 2026-03-12
Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Noah (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Ventana CTO), Samir Mehta (Infra lead), Priya Anand (Data ops)

Goal: understand compliance constraints and constraints for private deployment (VPC/on-prem) + target latency for real-time triage assistant (clinical notes summarization). They want a safe, auditable inference path and predictable per-patient throughput.

High-level requirements (verbatim bits and my clarifying notes):
- Data residency: all PHI must stay in their GCP project or on-prem airgapped node. No token logging externally. (they emphasized KMS/HSM integration)
- SLA: 99.9% availability for inference path during business hours (8am-8pm PT).
- Latency target: P95 < 350ms for 512-token context (note: samples from current pipeline show 300–800ms depending on batch).
- Throughput: baseline 10 concurrent sessions (avg 1.2 req/s per session during spikes up to 25 concurrent). Burst to 50 for 5–10m allowed.
- Model fidelity: prefer an Llama-3-class open model with medically tuned prompt templates. Want ability to A/B test a smaller quantized variant for cost savings.
- Auditability: must store request/response hashes + user IDs (not full PHI) to allow replay in private environment.
- Failover: when private capacity constrained, fallback to a redacted-hosted proxy is acceptable but only after explicit approval and only for non-PHI queries.

Immediate gotchas / risk flags:
- Network egress policies: Ventana's infra team uses restrictive VPC peering and requires pre-approved IP ranges. Tunnel/egress for any managed control plane will require legal/infra sign-off.
- KMS: They run Cloud HSM with strict key rotation; Redwood's KMS integration needs a design doc showing no plaintext key material leaves customer boundary.
- Audit logs: They want per-request signing (HMAC) recorded. Might need a lightweight sidecar to compute HMACs at ingress.
- Model caching: Their data contains repeating patient templates; caching KV prefixes could leak across tenants if not carefully isolated. Must verify one-KV-store-per-customer or namespaced keys for private托管.
- Regulatory: EU patients in their pipeline — if we route to hosted fallback, cross-border transfer rules may block it. Need a clear routing policy tied to region and patient residency metadata.

Operational notes / performance suspects:
- Their current preprocessor adds ~60ms per request (Python microservice on k8s) and does some redaction. We should recommend moving to Redwood edge preprocessor or provide a small Rust-based shim to reduce latency.
- Sequence lengths: median 300 tokens, but tail up to 1,800 tokens for long case notes. Need to size KV cache and memory for long tail. Suggest offering an LRU cache policy with limits annotated in SLO doc.
- Quantization: they are open to int8/4-bit for cost, but worried about hallucinations in clinical text. Recommend an eval run on a secured prompt set (we should request 200 anonymized prompts).

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Maya: draft KMS/HSM integration note for Ventana infra and how Redwood binds keys in VPC private deployment (due 2026-02-20).
- Noah: perf baseline run using their sample dataset (requesting 200 anonymized examples) to measure P50/P95/P99 across model variants (due 2026-02-25).
- Ventana (Samir): share list of allowed IP ranges + expected egress rules, plus sample k8s network policy (ETA 2026-02-18).
- Priya: provide 200 de-identified prompts and 20 edge-case long notes for hallucination / regression testing (ETA 2026-02-22).
- Maya + Legal: prepare a short note on fallback policy constraints and phrasing for acceptance in contract (first draft 2026-03-01).

Open questions (need answers to size design):
- Do they want request/response content stored at all? They said no PHI stored externally, but will accept hashes/hmacs. Need confirmation on whether hashed response + prompt is sufficient for their auditors.
- Which model family (exact) do they prefer? They mentioned "Llama-3-ish" but need explicit name and license constraints.
- Can they tolerate an intermediary sidecar for signing (adds ~10–15ms)?

Notes to self (quick):
- Bring up per-customer KV isolation during next SRE sync — remind infra about namespace collisions seen in previous private deploy.
- Ask Research for a short note on quantization impact on hallucination with medical prompts (maybe reuse existing internal eval).
- Add routing policy examples to the canary rollouts doc (product/hosted-api).

Follow-up meeting: schedule with Samir + Priya + Legal for KMS questions. Proposed times: 2026-02-19 10am PT or 2026-02-20 3pm PT.

Slack threads / refs: #ventana-intake (internal), CON-1789 (customer confluence — blank doc exists), JIRA-4521 (onramp epic).

Rough SLA thought: Initial private deployment w/ reserved capacity + autoscale buffer 2x baseline to handle bursts. Add canary fallback to quantized variant after 30 days of monitoring. Need cost sketch from finance (approx GPU hours / mo).

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya
summary: Working intake notes for Ventana Biotech private deployment. Captures compliance constraints (KMS/HSM), latency/throughput targets, audit/logging requirements, risks, and concrete action items. Requires sample prompts and IP/egress details from customer to finalize sizing.
